ops.title: the seeded tailscale authkey expires (~90d); how to recover/rename a stranded VM node
ops.body:
The single tailscale authkey in the sops blob (`tailscale/authkey`) is what every VM uses to JOIN the tailnet at first boot. It expires (~90 days). After expiry, already-joined VMs stay online (the node key persists; the authkey is only needed at join time), but any VM that must RE-JOIN (after `tailscale logout` or a device delete) cannot — `tailscale up --auth-key <expired>` fails and the VM is stranded offline.

hermes has no LAN sshd (`services.openssh.enable = false`, see [[macos-guest-vm-ops]]) and its runner uses `--serial-path=/dev/null --no-graphics`, so a stranded hermes has NO console/ssh path. `seedNodeConfig` (nixos/common.nix) is idempotent-once — it skips re-seeding once `/var/lib/sops-nix/key.txt` + `/var/lib/node-config/secrets.sops.yaml` exist — so a reboot alone re-runs `tailscale up` with the SAME stale key.

**Recovery (no host sops/age — use `nix run nixpkgs#sops`):**
1. Mint a fresh reusable key via the Tailscale API (`POST /api/v2/tailnet/-/keys`, `TAILSCALE_API_KEY` in repo `.env`).
2. `sops set` it into `tailscale/authkey` in BOTH blobs in-place (never decrypt→mv, see [[secret-handling-and-state-store]]): canonical `~/.yclaw/state/secrets.sops.yaml` and the Linux-VM share `~/.config/yclaw/vm-secrets/secrets.sops.yaml`. `SOPS_AGE_KEY_FILE=~/.yclaw/state/age/key.txt`. Back up + verify-decrypt first.
3. Force re-seed on the existing VM: `launchctl bootout gui/$UID/org.nixos.tart-<vm>` (KeepAlive would otherwise restart it), `hdiutil attach -nomount -readwrite ~/.tart/vms/<vm>/disk.img` → ext4 is `/dev/diskNs2` → `/opt/homebrew/opt/e2fsprogs/sbin/debugfs -w -R "rm /var/lib/node-config/secrets.sops.yaml" /dev/diskNs2` (fs must be `clean`) → `hdiutil detach` → `launchctl bootstrap gui/$UID ~/Library/LaunchAgents/org.nixos.tart-<vm>.plist`. On boot it re-seeds the fresh blob and autoconnect rejoins.

**Renaming a node (`hermes-1`→`hermes`), verified live 2026-07-07:** Tailscale DOES have a rename API — `POST /api/v2/device/<id>/name {"name":"hermes"}`. Delete the ghost device squatting the name (`DELETE /api/v2/device/<id>`), then rename the live node; MagicDNS + `tailscale ssh` follow immediately, NO reboot needed. (The old belief "no rename API, needs device-delete + reboot" was wrong.)

**Persistent-node MagicDNS drift:** since infra nodes became persistent (`ephemeral: false` in `_ts_mint_key`), old devices no longer self-reap — a disk-replace re-run joins as `<name>-1` while the dead record squats `<name>`, and every `tailscale ssh <name>` times out against the ghost. `deploy-vm.sh` always pre-deleted the old device; `bootstrap.sh` gained the same pre-delete on 2026-07-07 (commit 5d3418b) after a stranded recovery hit exactly this.
